bull_bear.body:
- IPO (listed Apr 17, 2026) proceeds earmarked partly for **long-term working capital** — to fund bid deposits, performance guarantees, mobilization for larger tenders. D/E 0.35x; Crisil upgraded to BBB+/Stable & A2 (Apr 28, 2026) post-IPO. No dividend/buyback discussed (maiden year).
- Working capital cycle ~75 days vs peers ~150 days — structural edge from PSU collection terms (80% of RA bills released in 30 days), efficient inventory, vendor negotiation. Retention money ~₹66 cr as of Mar'26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Order inflow deceleration** — OB declined Dec'25→Mar'26; if tender wins don't materialize, 50% growth guidance is at risk.
- **PSU/GETCO concentration** — 82% Gujarat, 82% PSU; single-utility and single-state dependence.
- **765kV / DISCOM are unproven** — eligibility claimed, not demonstrated.
- **Input shortages & price inflation** sector-wide; mitigated by price-variation clauses and advance bulk procurement, but execution timing risk remains.
- **Maiden-call optimism** — guidance unbacked by listed-company track record; H1-weak seasonality means front-loaded year could look soft.
- Underground cabling collapse in OB (₹10 cr) — recovery is a promise, not yet booked.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, founder-led (Patel family Chairman + MD). Kalpesh Patel cites 14 years GETCO relationship. Disclosure reasonably granular (vertical-level OB, collection terms, retention, GP/EBITDA bands, seasonality). Willingness to forgo low-margin private orders signals margin discipline. Some answers (UG cabling "recover in 3 months," 765kV eligibility) are aspirational and should be tracked for follow-through.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The real story is **working-capital arbitrage**: 75-day cycle vs ~150-day peers, funded by GETCO's fast PSU payments, is what drives the 44% ROCE — not engineering uniqueness. IPO money goes to working capital precisely to scale this edge to larger/longer tenders.
- **Revenue mix is shifting from "supply" to "execution"** — lowers material cost %, which mechanically flatters gross structure; watch that this is mix, not pricing.
- Mgmt directly compared itself to **Rajesh Power**, framing Om Power as EHV/overhead-transmission focused vs Rajesh's distribution tilt — a deliberate positioning of higher-voltage = higher-margin core.
- OB quality > OB size message: they'd rather hold ₹621 cr at protected margin than chase volume in low-margin private/other-state work.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "The April 2026 IPO raised ₹132.56 Cr of fresh capital. The proceeds position the Company for faster growth, support its historical pace of revenue growth at sustainable margins, and enhance its ability to bid for higher-value and more complex projects." (A separate tile states "₹133 Cr IPO fresh capital raised".)
- Leverage is presented as deliberately conservative: net debt-to-equity 0.35 in FY26, "from 0.59 in FY23", with interest coverage of 8.9x and a rated bank limit of ₹200 Cr.
- Credit progression tracks the deleveraging: CRISIL BB+ Stable / A4+ (2023) → BBB- Stable / A3 (2025) → BBB Stable / A3+ (Nov 2025, Pre-IPO) → BBB+ Stable / A2 (Apr 2026, Post-IPO).
- Total equity (FY26), pre-IPO, is stated at ₹137 Cr, with net asset value per share of ₹51.35 "from ₹17.63 in FY23".
- The deck states no dividend policy, payout ratio or buyback intention.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- 14+ years of execution track record; 1,000+ CKM of transmission lines and 11 substations commissioned
- Strong order book of Rs74,460.27 lakhs (Dec 31, 2025) across 58 projects
- GETCO 'AA Class' accreditation and ISO 9001/45001/14001 certifications
- Diversified client base spanning PSUs/state utilities and private renewable/industrial clients
- Rapid revenue and profit growth (FY23-FY25 revenue CAGR 52.45%, PAT CAGR 88.17%)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive-bidding dependence — Majority of projects awarded through competitive bidding; failure to qualify/win affects order inflow
- Customer/sector concentration — Heavy reliance on public-sector utilities (74.92% of FY25 revenue), especially GETCO in Gujarat
- Geographic concentration — Business historically concentrated in Gujarat; expansion to new states is nascent
- Working-capital intensity — EPC contracts tie up working capital in receivables and retention; increased reliance on borrowings
- Order-book execution risk — Order book may not convert to revenue on time; delays/penalties possible
- Raw material / third-party supply — Dependence on approved third-party vendors for towers, conductors, cables
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- No subsidiaries discussed; single operating entity. Four verticals (see header). Largest project to date: **Dholera 400kV GIS substation + multiple 400kV transmission lines across river, ~₹200 cr combined** — flagship, uses specialized Pile Foundation capability.
- Underground cabling revenue share fell (30% FY25 → ~20% FY26 → ~2% of OB) because existing projects were fully executed; mgmt insists pipeline (GETCO UG tenders) will refill it "in near 3 months."

business.body:
- "An integrated power-infrastructure EPC company delivering transmission lines, substations, underground cabling and O&M services up to 400 kV (eligible up to 765 kV)", incorporated 2011, listed on NSE and BSE in April 2026, headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
- The stated qualification moat is the "AA-class GETCO certification, the highest grade" — received for transmission lines & towers up to 400 kV in 2016 and for substations up to 400 kV in 2020, plus GETCO recognition as "Best EPC company" in 2017.
- Covers "all six stages in-house, from design to long-term O&M" (Engineering & Design, Procurement, Construction & Civil, Installation & Commissioning, Project Management & QA, Operation & Maintenance) as "Utilities increasingly award turnkey EPC contracts, and the market is shifting toward specialised, integrated players".
- Customer concentration is acknowledged and defended, not minimised: "Concentration is structural to utility EPC. The differentiator is the ability to qualify for complex projects, execute on-time, and manage working capital, project after project." Top-10 customers were 93% of FY26 revenue (vs 7% for the rest).
- Promoter-led and bootstrapped: "Three first-generation promoters with average 30+ years in the industry, who built the Company project-by-project", with 15+ years of company track record.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary] Proposed incorporation of OPTL Green Energy Private Limited to pursue renewable EPC opportunities — announced as a Q1FY27 development, described as "proposed", so not yet an operating entity on the deck's own wording.
- [Order momentum] "Order intake during the quarter remained healthy at ₹6,782 lakhs, including an order win from GETCO for the 220 kV Jantral AIS substation and a private sector order for a single-circuit 220 kV transmission line. The closing order book as on 30th June 2026 stood at ₹56,747 lakhs."
- [Post-period orders] "Subsequent to the quarter's close, the Company also received orders from PGVCL for a turnkey underground cable project and from GETCO for a 66 kV underground cable project".
- [Tendering risk flagged by management] "Tender activity from GETCO has been somewhat lumpy/muted at the start of the financial year, and we expect it to pick up as the year progresses"; separately, "Order intake in EPC is inherently lumpy. As the scale of operations and order book increase, inherent lumpiness will subside."
- [Customer mix] FY26 order book split PSU 82% / Private 18% and revenue mix PSU 83% / Private 17%; "Deeper private-sector work" with "Higher-margin captive and developer clients, aided by ROW capabilities" is a named growth avenue.

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA 12.72% (flat YoY). Q4 13.10% down from 17.5% base. GP held 23–25%.
- **Price variation clauses in nearly all POs** insulate from commodity inflation (conductors, insulators, breakers, transformers) — key margin defense amid sector-wide input shortages.
- Margin varies by project; specialized work (Pile Foundation) carries higher margin. Company walks away from low-margin private transmission work to protect blended margin.
- Material cost % of revenue fell — mgmt says due to more execution-led (vs supply-led) revenue mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **This quarter (Q4/FY26, maiden):** First listed-company call post-Apr'26 IPO. Record FY26 inflow ₹615 cr, OB ₹621 cr (all-time high), revenue +60.7%, PAT +81.2%, Crisil upgrade to BBB+/A2. Q4 margin normalized to 13.1% from a high 17.5% base. Underground cabling shrank to ~2% of OB. Dholera ₹200 cr flagship in execution.
- **Next-quarter / FY27 watch items:** (1) Q1 FY27 revenue vs implied weak-H1 (35%) seasonality; (2) order inflow recovery — does pipeline (>₹900 cr, 30–40% win rate) convert and reverse the Dec→Mar OB decline; (3) DISCOM distribution tender result (due ~next month); (4) underground cabling order refill ("3 months" promise); (5) first 765kV order/eligibility progress; (6) margin hold at 12–13% EBITDA / 8–9% PAT despite new-geography competition; (7) deployment of IPO working-capital proceeds.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** ~50%+ growth in FY27 (CFO explicitly confirmed "Yes" to 50%+; "same performance as last three fiscals").
- **Margins:** EBITDA 12–13%, PAT 8–9%, GP 23–25% — maintainable for next ~2 years per mgmt.
- **Seasonality:** H1 ~35% / H2 ~65% of revenue (back-half loaded).
- **Order inflow:** will be kept "commensurate" with 50% revenue growth, but NOT explicitly guided to 50% inflow growth — depends on tender wins & execution pace.
- **Watch:** No quarterly guidance given; verify Q1 FY27 against the implied weak-H1 (35%) seasonality.
outlook.title: Guidance (FY27 — next year, no separate next-quarter number given on maiden call)

outlook.body:
- **Year-end unexecuted order book ₹621 cr** (all-time high, 3x FY23, +41% YoY). By vertical: Transmission line ₹449 cr · Substation ₹140 cr · O&M ₹21 cr · Underground cabling only ₹10 cr (~2%).
- Post-quarter: ₹45 cr GETCO order (end-Apr) → effective OB ~₹665–670 cr.
- **Bid pipeline >₹900 cr** as of Mar 31, 2026; stated **win ratio 30–40%**.
- Client mix: 82% PSU / 18% private. Geography: Gujarat 82%; new states Rajasthan, Punjab, Dadra & Nagar Haveli; scouting 3–4 more pan-India.
- **Caution flag:** OB was ₹745 cr at Dec'25 (per RHP) vs ₹621 cr at Mar'26 → inflow slowed while execution sped up. Mgmt attributes to year-end tender timing.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **765kV upgrade cycle:** GETCO planning to move from 400kV to 765kV transmission lines & substations — Om Power has NO 765kV experience or order yet but claims 400kV track record makes it eligible. Genuine optionality, unproven.
- **11kV distribution / DISCOM:** entered 11kV ~2 years ago; participated in a DISCOM distribution tender, result expected "next month," targeting same 12–13% margin.
- **Geographic expansion:** Rajasthan, Punjab, DNH live; pan-India scouting.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light EPC model with no manufacturing. The supply portion of contracts (towers, conductors and conductor hardware, optical fibre cable, stringing accessories) is procured from approved third-party vendors against prescribed quality standards and voltage-class technical specifications; the service portion (detailed route survey, design, engineering, excavation, tower foundation, backfilling and levelling, erection of towers, stringing, testing, commissioning and statutory approvals) is executed in-house. The Company owns a significant portion of its execution machinery (tensioners and pullers, ferranas, hydraulic crimping machines, flories, winch machines, trucks and vehicles) and sources from third-party vendors for peak or specialised demand, maintaining inventories, equipment and machinery close to project sites. An in-house testing team with specialised equipment performs quality and performance tests across execution stages. Raw material inventory is held on a need basis as purchases are project-specific and grades vary by project. The Rajasthan substation project was awarded to a joint venture with Amarbhaw Power Private Limited.
